subject.title: Feature: Add 'private' groupPolicy option for Slack channels

question: Should Slack private-channel membership be accepted as a first-class group authorization boundary for triggering OpenClaw agents and tools?
rationale: The code change is bounded, but it changes Slack access-control semantics and the issue itself calls out Slack Connect/private shared-channel caveats.

options.title: Approve Slack-scoped private mode
options.body: Implement `groupPolicy: "private"` only for Slack with aligned routing, slash/action authorization, security audit guidance, docs, and tests while preserving existing defaults unless a migration is separately approved.

options.title: Reject private-channel boundary
options.body: Keep explicit Slack channel ID allowlists as the only non-open channel authorization mode and document private/shared channels as insufficient trust boundaries.

options.title: Defer to broader channel auth design
options.body: Track the idea under a broader channel authorization model if maintainers want a cross-channel policy rather than a Slack-specific value.

recommendation.title: Approve Slack-scoped private mode
recommendation.body: Implement `groupPolicy: "private"` only for Slack with aligned routing, slash/action authorization, security audit guidance, docs, and tests while preserving existing defaults unless a migration is separately approved.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already reviewed this exact issue and has recent Slack/config history, while the remaining blocker is a security/product boundary decision.
